originalTitle: Many earlier diagonal barriers share one current ghost capacity
originalHypotheses: Canonical positive-MEX/COPY recurrence and the named banked lemmas in the source.
independence: Proof reconstructed from primary arguments and explicit definitions. Earlier source status/review assertions were not treated as proof. The author previously collected these sources; the present derivations and finite/exact-algebra checks are new independent audit work.
detailedDerivation: For owner b<q, M=d(b), q≤M<d(q), the hosts<h=b having M in their start-q journal are exactly its H(b) prebirth services plus G_b(q) postbirth services. Birth occurs only at b, inherited seed membership at h<b is impossible, and private nonreuse makes all such hosts distinct.
If M is absent now, each blocker M<x<d(q) has a genuine recomputed current cell by coverage and x>q. At a host<h=b, MEX forces M into its journal because M is absent from the full current prefix.
These lower hosts have capacity H+G; hosts b,…,q−1 add at mostq−b. Birth column q is diagonal. Absence therefore implies A(d(q))−A(M)≤H(b)+G_b(q)+q−b.
Contraposition forces every violating owner’s distinct diagonal into an actual current ghost cell. Row injectivity bounds their number by I(q)=2q+1−d(q)−H(q).
Finally G_b(q)≤q−b−1 gives MB3. The guard M≥q is essential to rule out frozen blocker cells; the theorem does not certify joint history/placement feasibility.
